question: Does allowing dead knots in a start make it easier for a part to return and give parts off; is a part that returns always made of knots that waited; and can the round a knot was made in be read from that knot's own holdings?
inputs: The registered census of 86,032 starts and the named families; the shared definitions; ticket A's engine after its gate.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze; for the engine's author, the pilot's programs.
primary_observable: For every run the kind of outcome, the first return with its rounds and parts, and which members waited; for the rings and the generator, each knot's round, parents and fresh distinctions.
comparators_or_controls: Ordinary growth on every start; two realisations of each cycle through dead knots; laws without waiting.
resource_budget: The census through the shared runner, at most 16 GB and one row in the long-running index; everything else under ten minutes.
first_executable_signal: Row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column.
stop_rule: The study stops when its registered runs are done and each prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of laws changed by hand (assumption A224) and of starts built by hand; every census and sample is finite and proves no all-size statement; no claim about ordinary growth beyond the cited records, and none about time, minds or living things.
